blocks.heading: Nine Paths Is Still Too Many

items.text: Do you want a case-and-group MBA classroom, a reading-and-argument-heavy law degree, a data-and-modelling-heavy Economics program, or a skill-first route where a portfolio matters more than a syllabus, like UX or data analytics.
A course with a great salary ceiling that fights how you actually like to work will not survive the years it demands from you.

blocks.heading: Why Stacking Beats Picking Only One Course
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Why stacking beats picking only one course

rows: MA Economics or MA Public Policy
Data visualisation and one statistical tool (R, Python, or advanced Excel)
Turns a pure research or theory profile into someone consulting firms and think tanks can actually deploy on live data, which is where the higher-paying roles sit.
3-year LLB
CLAT-PG and an LLM in a specific domain (IP, tax, or tech law)
A generalist LLB caps out faster than a specialised LLM. The specialisation, not the degree alone, is what firms pay a premium for.
PG Diploma in Journalism and Mass Communication
One demonstrated digital or social-strategy skill, SEO, analytics reading, or short-form video editing
Newsroom hiring has shrunk while digital and brand-newsroom hiring has grown. The pivot skill is what keeps the journalism training relevant to where the jobs actually are now.
Digital marketing certification
One real, finished campaign with reported numbers, plus depth in one paid channel
Employers do not hire the certificate. They hire the one campaign you can walk them through with actual spend, reach, and conversion numbers attached.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Government law colleges charge roughly Rs 10,000-50,000 a year, and private colleges commonly run Rs 1-5 lakh a year, with entry now largely through CUET PG or a university's own law entrance test. Corporate law is one of the higher-paying entry fields once qualified: freshers can expect roughly Rs 40,000-80,000 a month at a strong firm, translating to Rs 4-10 LPA depending on the employer and city.

Law is the path most guides skip when talking about BA graduates, because CLAT itself is usually associated with 5-year integrated courses for 12th-pass students. A BA graduate's actual route runs through a 3-year LLB first.

blocks.heading: 3. MA Economics: the Quant-Heavy Route

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Delhi School of Economics reports salary packages between Rs 7-22 LPA with an average around Rs 11 LPA, placing students into business analysis, investment banking, and economic research roles at firms like Goldman Sachs, American Express, and Nomura. JNU blends the same mathematical training with development-economics and policy work, and its highest reported off-campus placement has touched roughly Rs 33 LPA.

The same MA Economics degree from a general, lower-ranked university typically starts closer to Rs 4-6 LPA. The subject is not what commands the premium here. The specific college, and the quantitative rigour it forces on you, is what does.

Pure reporting pay stays modest for years without a deliberate move. The graduates who clear Rs 8-15 LPA within a few years are almost always the ones who pivoted into digital editorial leadership, brand journalism, or media-business roles, not the ones who stayed purely on the reporting beat.
